facts.fact: BCEAO told every bank, e-money issuer and payment institution in the WAEMU to be connected to PI-SPI by 30 June 2026, then on 25 June 2026 moved the deadline to 30 September 2026 (microfinance 30 June 2027); the union includes Cote d'Ivoire, which had 23 integrated participants by late July (iAfrikan, 29 Sep 2026).

facts.fact: The UMOA Banking Commission's 2025 report counts 18 licensed e-money issuers (EME) in the union, 4 of them in Cote d'Ivoire, with Djogana Pay newly approved in Cote d'Ivoire in 2025; these are non-bank issuers licensed under BCEAO rules (Horonya Finance, 27 Aug 2026).

BCEAO communique of 25 June 2026 set 30 September 2026 as the deadline for banks, e-money institutions and payment institutions of the UEMOA to connect to PI-SPI, and 30 June 2027 for microfinance institutions; Cote d'Ivoire had 23 authorised participants at 31 July 2026 (Finance SAO, 18 Aug 2026).

facts.fact: BCEAO instruction no. 001-01-2024, applied since January 2024, obliges all fintechs offering payment services in the WAEMU, which includes Cote d'Ivoire, to obtain a licence or stop; the deadline was extended to 31 August 2025 (TechCabal, 17 Feb 2026).

BCEAO instruction no. 001-01-2024 licenses payment institutions that are not banks at three tiers by capital (CFA 10, 20 or 100 million), valid across the eight WAEMU states including Cote d'Ivoire; 20 payment institutions held a licence union-wide by September 2025 (TechCabal, 17 Feb 2026).

The instruction obliges fintechs to hold a licence, with capital of 10 to 100 million FCFA, and four providers were licensed in Cote d'Ivoire by 27 May 2025.

The BCEAO approved SycaPay, Firstcom Global Payments, Julaya and InTouch as payment institutions in Cote d'Ivoire under the instruction.
